title: The new National Gallery of Canada building opens in Ottawa.
text: The National Gallery of Canada, located in the capital city of Ottawa, Ontario, is Canada's national art museum. The museum's building takes up 46,621 square metres (501,820 sq ft), with 12,400 square metres (133,000 sq ft) of space used for exhibiting art.

title: Morley Callaghan – A Wild Old Man on the Road
text: Edward Morley Callaghan was a Canadian novelist, short story writer, playwright, and TV and radio personality.

title: Jeffrey Simpson – Spoils of Power
text: Jeffrey Carl Simpson, OC, is a Canadian journalist. Simpson was The Globe and Mail's national affairs columnist for almost three decades.

title: bill bissett – What We Have
text: Bill Bissett, commonly stylised as bill bissett, is a Canadian poet known for his unconventional style especially regarding unusual orthography and the use of visual elements.

title: See 1988 Governor General's Awards for a complete list of winners and finalists for those awards.
text: Each winner of the 1988 Governor General's Awards for Literary Merit received $5000 and a medal from the Governor General of Canada. The winners and nominees were selected by a panel of judges administered by the Canada Council for the Arts.

title: Books in Canada First Novel Award: Marion Quednau, The Butterfly Chair
text: The Amazon Canada First Novel Award, formerly the Amazon.ca First Novel Award and the Books in Canada First Novel Award, is a Canadian literary award, co-presented by Amazon.ca and The Walrus to the best first novel in English published the previous year by a citizen or resident of Canada. It has been awarded since 1976.

title: Geoffrey Bilson Award: 1988 – Carol Matas, 'Lisa
text: The Geoffrey Bilson Award for Historical Fiction for Young People is a Canadian literary award that goes to the best work of historical fiction written for youth each year. The award is named after Geoffrey Bilson, a writer of historical fiction for youth and a history professor at the University of Saskatchewan who died suddenly in 1987.

title: Gerald Lampert Award: Di Brandt, Questions I Asked My Mother
text: The Gerald Lampert Memorial Award is an annual literary award presented by the League of Canadian Poets to the best volume of poetry published by a first-time poet. It is presented in honour of poetry promoter Gerald Lampert.

title: Marian Engel Award: Edna Alford
text: The Writers' Trust Engel/Findley Award is a Canadian literary award, presented by the Writers' Trust of Canada to an established Canadian author to honour their body of work. Presented for the first time in 2008 under the name Notable Author Award, the award was created by merging the formerly separate Marian Engel Award and Timothy Findley Award, which were presented to female and male nominees respectively.

title: Pat Lowther Award: Gwendolyn MacEwen, Afterworlds
text: The Pat Lowther Memorial Award is an annual Canadian literary award presented by the League of Canadian Poets to the year's best book of poetry by a Canadian woman. The award was established in 1980 to honour poet Pat Lowther, who was murdered by her husband in 1975.

title: Stephen Leacock Award: Paul Quarrington, King Leary
text: Paul Lewis Quarrington was a Canadian novelist, playwright, screenwriter, filmmaker, musician, and educator.

title: Trillium Book Award: Timothy Findley, Stones
text: The Trillium Book Award is an annual literary award presented to writers in Ontario, Canada. It is administered by Ontario Creates, a Crown agency of the Government of Ontario, which is overseen by the Ministry of Heritage, Sport, Tourism and Culture Industries.

title: Vicky Metcalf Award: Barbara Smucker
text: The Vicky Metcalf Award for Literature for Young People, colloquially called the Vicky, is given annually at the Writers' Trust Awards to a writer or illustrator whose body of work has been "inspirational to Canadian youth". It is a top honour for Canadian children's writers and Canadian children's book illustrators.
wiki: Vicky Metcalf Award for Literature for Young People

title: “Faith” by George Michael
text: "Faith" is a song by English singer and songwriter George Michael. Written and produced by Michael, it was released via Columbia Records and Epic Records as the second single from his 1987 debut solo album of the same name.

title: “Got My Mind Set on You” by George Harrison
text: "Got My Mind Set on You" Set on You") is a song written and composed by Rudy Clark and originally recorded by James Ray in 1962, under the title "I've Got My Mind Set on You". An edited version of the song was released later in the year as a single on Dynamic Sound Records credited to Ray with Hutch Davie Orchestra & Chorus.

listen: Got My Mind Set on You George Harrison

title: “Could've Been” by Tiffany
text: "Could've Been" is a song by American teen-pop artist Tiffany, released as the third single from her debut album, Tiffany. The track was written by Lois Blaisch and produced by George Tobin.

title: “Pump Up the Volume” by M|A|R|R|S
text: "Pump Up the Volume" is the only single by British recording act M|A|R|R|S. The song was written by Martyn Young and Steve Young, and produced by the former and John Fryer. It was recorded in 1987 and released on 3 August of the same year.

title: “Never Gonna Give You Up” by Rick Astley
text: "Never Gonna Give You Up" is a song by English singer Rick Astley, released on 27 July 1987. The song is widely regarded as Astley's most popular, as well as his signature song, and it is often played at the end of his live concerts.
listen: Never Gonna Give You Up Rick Astley

title: “Get Outta My Dreams, Get into My Car” by Billy Ocean
text: "Get Outta My Dreams, Get into My Car" is a song by the Trinidadian-British singer Billy Ocean, based on a line in the Sherman Brothers' song "You're Sixteen". It was released as the first single from Ocean's seventh studio album, Tear Down These Walls.

listen: Get Outta My Dreams, Get into My Car Billy Ocean

title: “Wishing Well” by Terence Trent D'Arby
text: "Wishing Well" is a song by American singer-songwriter Terence Trent D'Arby. Written by D'Arby and Sean Oliver, D'Arby said "Wishing Well" was written "when I was in a half-asleep, half-awake state of mind", and that he "liked the feel of the words".

title: “Always on My Mind” by Pet Shop Boys
text: "Always on My Mind" is a ballad written by Wayne Carson, Johnny Christopher, and Mark James, first recorded by Brenda Lee and first released by Gwen McCrae in March 1972. Lee's version was released three months later in June 1972.
listen: Always on My Mind Pet Shop Boys

title: “Beds Are Burning” by Midnight Oil
text: "Beds Are Burning" is a song by the Australian rock band Midnight Oil, the first track from their sixth album, Diesel and Dust. This song was released as the second single from the album.

title: “One More Try” by George Michael
text: "One More Try" is a song recorded by English singer and songwriter George Michael from his debut solo album, Faith. It was released on 11 April 1988 as the album's fourth single by Columbia Records.

title: “Together Forever” by Rick Astley
text: "Together Forever" is a song recorded by English singer-songwriter Rick Astley and released by RCA and BMG in February 1988, as the fourth single from his debut album, Whenever You Need Somebody. The song was both written and produced by Stock Aitken Waterman, and reached number two in the United Kingdom, behind Neighbours star and fellow SAW artist Kylie Minogue's debut single "I Should Be So Lucky".

title: “New Sensation” by INXS
text: "New Sensation" is a song by Australian rock group INXS. It was the third single released from their sixth studio album, Kick (1987). The music was composed by Andrew Farriss and the lyrics were written by Michael Hutchence.

title: “The Flame” by Cheap Trick
text: "The Flame" is a song by the American rock band Cheap Trick, released in 1988 as the first single from their 10th album, Lap of Luxury. The power ballad was written by songwriters Bob Mitchell and Nick Graham and was produced by Richie Zito.

title: “Roll with It” by Steve Winwood
text: "Roll with It" is a song recorded by Steve Winwood for his album Roll with It, released on Virgin Records. It was written by Winwood and long-time collaborator Will Jennings.

title: “I Don't Wanna Go On with You Like That” by Elton John
text: "I Don't Wanna Go On with You Like That" is a song by British musician Elton John and lyricist Bernie Taupin, performed by John. It is from his twenty-first studio album, Reg Strikes Back, and was released as its lead single by Rocket and MCA Records.
wiki: I Don't Wanna Go On with You Like That
listen: I Don't Wanna Go On with You Like That Elton John

title: “Fast Car” by Tracy Chapman
text: "Fast Car" is a song by American singer-songwriter Tracy Chapman, released as her debut single on April 6, 1988, by Elektra Records. It served as the lead single from her 1988 self-titled debut studio album.

title: “Perfect World” by Huey Lewis and the News
text: "Perfect World" is a song performed by Huey Lewis and the News and released as the first single from the album Small World in late June 1988. The single peaked at number three on the US Billboard Hot 100 and #48 on the UK Singles Chart.
wiki: Perfect World (Huey Lewis and the News song)

title: “Monkey” by George Michael
text: "Monkey" is a song by the English singer and songwriter George Michael. It was released as a single in 1988 and reached number-one on the US Billboard Hot 100 and number 13 on the UK singles chart.

title: “It Would Take a Strong Strong Man” by Rick Astley
text: "It Would Take a Strong Strong Man" is a 1987 song by English singer-songwriter Rick Astley. Written by Stock Aitken Waterman, it was released as the fifth single from Astley's debut album Whenever You Need Somebody.
wiki: It Would Take a Strong Strong Man
listen: It Would Take a Strong Strong Man Rick Astley

title: “One Good Woman” by Peter Cetera
text: "One Good Woman" is a song by Peter Cetera, formerly the lead singer of the rock band Chicago. Cetera co-wrote and co-produced the track with Patrick Leonard, and the song was included on Cetera's third studio album, One More Story.

title: Adrienne Clarkson Presents
text: Adrienne Clarkson Presents is a Canadian cultural entertainment series broadcast on CBC Television beginning in 1988. The series ended in 1999, the year host Adrienne Clarkson was appointed Governor General of Canada.

title: Mount Royal
text: Mount Royal is a Canadian prime time television soap opera that aired on CTV. It premiered January 3, 1988 with a two-hour episode. The series starred Patrick Bauchau and Domini Blythe.

title: My Secret Identity
text: My Secret Identity is a television series starring Jerry O'Connell and Derek McGrath. Originally broadcast from October 9, 1988 to May 25, 1991 on CTV in Canada, the series also aired in syndication in the United States.

title: Tickle on the Tum
text: Tickle on the Tum is a series of ten-minute programmes for young children produced by Granada Television and aired on the ITV network from 5 November 1984 until 29 November 1988. The series was set in the General Store and Post Office in the fictional village of Tickle-on-the-Tum.

title: Zardip's Search for Healthy Wellness
text: Zardip's Search for Healthy Wellness is a Canadian educational television show from the 1980s intended to teach public health messages to children. The show's 13 episode arc featured Zardip Pacific, played by Keram Malicki-Sánchez, a robot alien from a planet whose robot inhabitants are breaking down as they do not know how to live a healthy lifestyle.

title: The Ghosts of Motley Hall
text: The Ghosts of Motley Hall is a British children's television series written by Richard Carpenter. It was produced and directed by Quentin Lawrence for Granada Television, and broadcast between 1976 and 1978 on the ITV network.

title: Learning The Ropes
text: Learning the Ropes is a Canadian-produced sitcom that aired on CTV in Canada and in syndication in the United States from September 1988 to March 1989. The series stars Lyle Alzado as Robert Randall, a teacher who works as a professional wrestler in the evening.

title: Electric Circus
text: Electric Circus is a Canadian live dance music television program that aired on MuchMusic and Citytv from September 16, 1988, to December 12, 2003. The name originated from a nightclub that once existed at Citytv's first studio at 99 Queen Street East in Toronto.

title: MovieTelevision
text: MovieTelevision is a Canadian entertainment news series, which aired on Citytv from 1988 to 2006. The series aired reports on film, including interviews with actors and filmmakers, preview clips of upcoming films and coverage of film-related events such as the Toronto International Film Festival.

title: La Course destination monde
text: La Course destination monde is a Canadian reality competition television series, which aired on Télévision de Radio-Canada from 1988 to 1999. The series was a filmmaking competition which sent young emerging filmmakers from Quebec around the world to make short films about their destinations, with prizes awarded at the conclusion of each season to the best films coming out of the competition.
